title: Docs: Add AI section
body:
## What I did

Adds a docs section for AI-related features, like the component/docs manifests and MCP server.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### Manual testing

1. Preview the docs here: https://deploy-preview-381--storybook-frontpage.netlify.app/docs/10.3/ai
1. _Or_ sync this branch with locally running docs site

### Documentation

<!-- Please check (put an "x" inside the "[ ]") the applicable items below to indicate which documentation has been updated. -->

- [x] Add or update documentation reflecting your changes
- [ ] If you are deprecating/removing a feature, make sure to update
      [MIGRATION.MD](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/MIGRATION.md)

## Checklist for Maintainers

- [x] When this PR is ready for testing, make sure to add `ci:normal`, `ci:merged` or `ci:daily` GH label to it to run a specific set of sandboxes. The particular set of sandboxes can be found in `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/sandbox-templates.ts`
- [x] Make sure this PR contains **one** of the labels below:
   <details>
     <summary>Available labels</summary>

  - `bug`: Internal changes that fixes incorrect behavior.
  - `maintenance`: User-facing maintenance tasks.
  - `dependencies`: Upgrading (sometimes downgrading) dependencies.
  - `build`: Internal-facing build tooling & test updates. Will not show up in release changelog.
  - `cleanup`: Minor cleanup style change. Will not show up in release changelog.
  - `documentation`: Documentation **only** changes. Will not show up in release changelog.
  - `feature request`: Introducing a new feature.
  - `BREAKING CHANGE`: Changes that break compatibility in some way with current major version.
  - `other`: Changes that don't fit in the above categories.

   </details>

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Comprehensive AI/MCP documentation added (best practices, MCP server overview, API, manifests, sharing, tooling).
  * New built-in manifest tag to control story inclusion.
  * Installer/configuration snippets and CLI usage examples for MCP tooling.
  * New main-config feature flags documented: componentsManifest and experimentalCodeExamples.

* **Documentation**
  * Numerous CSF 3/CSF Next story and addon configuration examples.
  * AI/MCP pages added and sidebar ordering updated to surface AI content.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

```suggestion
Alternatively, you can apply the same content with a JSDoc comment above the component export.
```

1. No, the parameters-driven API is not ported over to manifest generation.
2. I think we should document component-first comments and not meta-first comments. Most descriptions are valuable both for agents, Storybook consumers and internal developlers. Comments above the components will target all of these naturally, as internal developers and package consumers will see the descriptions on component-export hover in the IDEs. Comments above meta is considered more of an escape hatch, if you have some specific need for the description in Storybook UI/manifests to be _different_ from the default description you have for the component.

comments.author: JReinhold
comments.body:
This page is missing instructions on how to add summaries to components and docs entries. Summaries are the texts that shows up in the `list-all-documentation` tool next to each entry (and next to stories in components' "Other Stories" section), and so they are an important tool to help the agent decide which of the docs/components are relevant for the given task (however we haven't scientifically confirmed _how important_ summaries are). When no summaries are provided, the first 90 chars of the descriptions are used instead.

component (also works for stories):

```jsx
/**
 * This is the description. it's great.
 *  
 * @summary this is the summary for the component. it's shorter, but also great.
 */
export const Button = () {...};
```

mdx:

```mdx
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

<Meta
  title="the title"
  summary="the summary"
/>
```

LMK if you need more info

comments.author: JReinhold
comments.body:
You haven't described the `get-documentation-for-story` tool in the docs toolset.

`get-documentation` only returns the first three stories for a component, to not bloat the context. However at the end of the tool is an `## Other Stories` section that lists the remaining stories with their id, name and summaries. Based on this, the agent can choose to get information about these stories using the `get-documentation-for-story` tool.

🌐 Web query:

`top-level await CommonJS TypeScript Node.js compatibility`

💡 Result:

- **Node.js:** Top-level `await` is an **ESM feature**. In Node, **CommonJS `require()` can only load synchronous ES modules**; if the required module (or anything it imports) uses top-level `await`, Node throws **`ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`**. ([nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v23.11.1/docs/api/esm.html?utm_source=openai))  
- **TypeScript:** TypeScript only allows top-level `await` when `target` is **`es2017`+** and `module` is a module kind that supports it (e.g. **`es2022`/`esnext`/`system`/`node16`/`nodenext`**). **`module: "commonjs"` does not support top-level `await`.** ([typescript.p2hp.com](https://typescript.p2hp.com/docs/handbook/release-notes/overview.html?utm_source=openai))  
- **Interoperability note:** Even with modern Node/TypeScript improvements to “`require()` of ESM”, Node **still does not permit** `require()` of ESM that contains top-level `await`. ([devblogs.microsoft.com](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-5-8/?utm_source=openai))  

**What to do**
1. **If you want top-level `await`: use ESM output**
   - `package.json`: set `"type": "module"` (or use `.mjs`)
   - `tsconfig.json`: use e.g.
     - `"module": "nodenext"` (or `"node16"`, `"esnext"`)
     - `"target": "es2022"` (or at least `"es2017"`) ([typescriptlang.org](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/theory.html?utm_source=openai))  
2. **If you must stay CommonJS:** you can’t use top-level `await`; use an **async function/IIFE** or **dynamic `import()`** from async code instead. ([nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.11.0/docs/api/modules.html?utm_source=openai))

Citations:

- 1: https://nodejs.org/download/release/v23.11.1/docs/api/esm.html?utm_source=openai
- 2: https://typescript.p2hp.com/docs/handbook/release-notes/overview.html?utm_source=openai
- 3: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-5-8/?utm_source=openai
- 4: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/theory.html?utm_source=openai
- 5: https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.11.0/docs/api/modules.html?utm_source=openai
